correctness.rationale: Domination means no unused row and unused column simultaneously; induced rook connectivity equals connectivity of selected incidence edges. Deleting cycle edges and then full-side tree leaves forces a minimal set to be a tree spanning exactly one bipartition side. If the other side has a leaf, its edge can be removed; otherwise every deletion disconnects edges or loses full-side occupancy. The weighted bipartite matrix-tree identity counts trees by column degree, and positive-exponent extraction is b! Stirling(m-1,b), giving both sums and the two integer size intervals. The standard connected labeled graph exponential formula establishes the full EGF. An independently written subset-and-BFS enumerator verified full and minimal counts on four boards including 3x4: 2x2 {2:4}, 2x4 {2:4,4:2}, 3x3 {3:6,4:36}, 3x4 {3:4,4:39,5:72}. Finite cases supplement the all-parameter proof.
residual_risks: Does not prove similar characterizations for arbitrary line graphs; only m,n>=2 minimal-size theorem.

value.rationale: Connected domination is a natural graph polynomial not determined by the ordinary one. The complete characterization and Stirling-number size enumerator yield a sharp cardinality gap for minimum-by-inclusion sets on all rectangular rook graphs, an intrinsic usable extremal and enumerative fact.
residual_risks: Unlabeled isomorphism classes and other graph families are not addressed.

final_claim: For K_m square K_n (m,n>=2), the complete connected-domination EGF is (exp(u)+exp(v)-1)(log F-u-v) with F=sum (1+z)^(ab)u^a v^b/(a!b!). Inclusion-minimal connected dominating sets are precisely one-sided-spanning bipartite incidence trees with no leaves on the incomplete side; the exact Stirling polynomial and two-interval size spectrum have a gap iff max(m,n)>=2 min(m,n).
limitations: m,n>=2 for minimal-set classification; simple labeled rook graphs only.
Ordinary rook domination and standard matrix-tree/exponential enumeration are prior tools.
